payload.selection_rationale: One proposal (practice), selected as the core. It fits what the survey measured: SL-043 is mostly built, and the proposal designs only the three residuals the survey named. (a) The link rule is a tag list, not the surrogate-bit rule. (b) The used-space figure exists only in the App. (c) The tests the agreed criteria name are missing. Criteria 2 and 3 are cut as present and are not redesigned. The classifier change is backed by the risk spike, which walked 829K directories of C: with exactly this descend rule through the project's own DirectoryReader and saw only errors 5, 363 and 1920. It is also the ONLY-UNDER condition of U-004. The volume figure resolves the survey's O-031 contradiction by keeping O-031's guarantee (nothing in the scan waits on the read) and moving where the read lives. The source is the GetDiskFreeSpaceExW route the spike bracketed against Get-Volume (30 of 30 inside, median 0 B). I kept the proposal's shape and changed the seam where its own guarantee was weakest. The thread it started captured the ScanStore, so a stalled share would pin a store whose budget is ~700 MiB. The thread now captures only the completion source. I added a test and a rule for "the scan never waits on the figure", which the proposal asserted but nothing pinned. The proposal's output was clipped before any over_engineering_flag or expert list, so none is visible to me. No project-scope stack was decided here: everything used (C#, P/Invoke, xUnit, powershell.exe inside one test) is already inside the recorded stack.

components.name: EntryClassifier link rule
components.responsibility: Criterion 4. Classify returns Link only when (attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT) != 0 AND (tag & 0x20000000) != 0. Every other entry is Folder or File from the directory attribute: cloud tags 0x9000201A/401A/601A/E01A, reparse with tag 0, DFS 0x8000000A, and any other non-surrogate tag. The explicit MOUNT_POINT/SYMLINK/DFS match at EntryClassifier.cs:24-33 is removed. The attribute is tested first and the tag is never read when it is clear, because the fallback listing class carries EaSize in that field.
components.key_interactions: Both listing classes already pass (attributes, tag). Scanner.cs:166 queues only Folder and Scanner.cs:225-227 returns before a Link is queued; both are unchanged, and so are HardlinkTests and LinkTests, whose junction and symlink tags stay surrogate. A descended non-surrogate folder that fails to open goes through the existing FolderDone path (Scanner.cs:156-160) and is recorded Unreadable with its code. ArchitectureRulesTests.OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute and its fitness.yaml twin still hold because the change stays in this file.

components.name: Native declarations
components.responsibility: Add a named constant for the name-surrogate bit (0x20000000, after winnt.h's IsReparseTagNameSurrogate) and a GetDiskFreeSpaceExW P/Invoke. The IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT/_SYMLINK/_DFS constants at Kernel32.cs:30-32 stay for the table test's inputs. The classifier no longer reads them.
components.key_interactions: Read by EntryClassifier (bit) and VolumeSpace (P/Invoke). The P/Invoke lives here so Scanning makes no BCL file-system call.

components.name: VolumeSpace
components.responsibility: Criterion 6. IsDriveRoot(root): after stripping \\?\, the root is exactly one drive letter, a colon and a backslash (letter case-insensitive). This is the App's current rule moved, not widened. Start(root, TaskCompletionSource<long?> figure, reader = default) completes figure with null at once when the root is not a drive root. Otherwise it runs the reader on a dedicated named background thread (IsBackground, not the pool, so a stalled redirector parks one thread and no pool worker). The default reader calls GetDiskFreeSpaceExW on the STRIPPED 'X:\' form the spike measured and returns TotalNumberOfBytes - TotalNumberOfFreeBytes. A false return or any exception completes the figure with null, never a faulted task. The thread's closure captures only the completion source, the stripped root and the reader. It must not reference ScanStore, so a read that never returns cannot pin a scan's memory.
components.key_interactions: Called once by Scanner at scan start. It uses TrySetResult, so a double completion is a no-op. It uses no DriveInfo, so TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:67-72) and its fitness.yaml twin hold unchanged.

components.name: Scanner start hook
components.responsibility: At scan start, call VolumeSpace.Start with the store's completion source, so drive-root scans start the read and folder scans complete with null. Nothing on the walk, cancel or end-of-scan path awaits, waits on or reads the figure. This is all of O-031's guarantee and it is kept. The reader is an optional internal parameter, so a test can substitute a blocking reader and a real scan of a drive root can be shown to end while the figure is still pending.
components.key_interactions: No new field on ScanResult. The figure hangs off the store, which the App already holds.

components.name: ScanStore volume figure
components.responsibility: Holds the figure alongside the tree: a TaskCompletionSource<long?> created in the constructor with RunContinuationsAsynchronously, exposed as Task<long?> VolumeUsed. An internal accessor hands the completion source (not a method group on the store, which would capture it) to Scanner and VolumeSpace. It costs one object per scan and nothing per row, well inside SL-042's ~136 MiB headroom.
components.key_interactions: The Task is created before the scan starts, so it is never null. It has three states: null result (answered, no figure), value, and pending (a read that has not returned). Nothing in Core awaits it.

components.name: App outcome reads the scan's figure
components.responsibility: Delete VolumeInUse (MainWindow.xaml.cs:252-271). The existing post-scan work on its own thread (:186-194) takes store.VolumeUsed instead of calling DriveInfo, and keeps whatever blocking structure it has now, so a pending figure never blocks the UI thread or the next scan. ShowOutcome/Coverage (:383-484) keep their text and their 'did not fail at the root' condition. Null and pending both mean no figure is shown. DriveInfo stays in the App for the drive list.
components.key_interactions: Without this consumer, Core would record a number nobody reads, which is this project's commonest defect shape. The App opens no new path, so the long-path no-go does not require app.manifest in this slice. --report schema 1 is unchanged.

components.name: Classifier table rows
components.responsibility: Criterion 4 check. The table uses literal attribute/tag values, both for directory and file where they apply. Link rows: 0xA0000003, 0xA000000C, 0xA000001D file, 0xA0000010 dir. Descend rows: 0x9000201A, 0x9000401A, 0x9000601A, 0x9000E01A, tag 0 with the reparse attribute, and DFS 0x8000000A dir. Two rows flip rather than disappear: DFS dir Link -> Folder (:20) and 0xA000001D file File -> Link (:24). One row has a surrogate-looking tag value with the reparse attribute clear, which must not be a Link.
components.key_interactions: grep the tests for other assertions that encode the old tag list, such as ListingFallbackTests and RootTests, before finishing.

components.name: Independent-listing long-path test + token helper
components.responsibility: Criterion 1 check. The first statement asserts the process token is NOT elevated and fails, never skips. The helper opens the process token with TOKEN_QUERY and calls GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation=20) with a 4-byte buffer (the spike's 256-byte buffer gave ERROR_BAD_LENGTH), throwing Win32Exception on failure. The test builds a link-free tree under %TEMP% through \\?\ paths: several levels of ~40-character segments so folders and files cross 260 and the deepest path exceeds 400, a few files per level, one hidden file and one hidden folder. It scans the tree and rebuilds each entry's path from its parent chain. The reference is Directory.EnumerateFileSystemEntries(\\?\root, "*", new EnumerationOptions{RecurseSubdirectories=true, AttributesToSkip=0, IgnoreInaccessible=false, MatchType=Simple}). It asserts ordinal set equality, store count == distinct count == listing count, and status Completed.
components.key_interactions: The spike measured testhost at Medium integrity, TokenIsElevated=0, in 2 of 2 valid runs. The tree has no links, so the reference's own recursion policy on reparse points never enters the comparison.

components.name: Read-error classification rows
components.responsibility: Criterion 5 check as agreed. A Theory over Scanner.ClassifyReadError: 5, 363 and 1920 give Unreadable with and without a cancel requested; 995 gives Cancelled only when a cancel is requested. It extends the existing 0/5/995 test beside it. UnreadableFolderTests' ACL-deny test stays as the real-tree case for error 5.

components.name: Volume figure tests
components.responsibility: Criterion 6 check. (1) System drive: root = Path.GetPathRoot(Environment.SystemDirectory). Read G1 from Get-Volume, start the scan, await store.VolumeUsed with a 30 s bound (must be non-null), cancel, read G2, await the scan's end with a bound, and assert the figure is unchanged and within [min(G1,G2)-64 MiB, max(G1,G2)+64 MiB]. (2) A folder scan under %TEMP% completes VolumeUsed with null immediately. (3) An IsDriveRoot table. (4) A drive letter with no volume completes null, not faulted. (5) A substituted reader that blocks: a scan of the drive root started with it ends Cancelled while VolumeUsed is still pending. Get-Volume is read by powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive printing [long](Size - SizeRemaining).
components.key_interactions: Test 5 is the only thing that pins O-031's reason for existing. Every wait in these tests has a bound, so a scan that fails to cancel fails the test instead of hanging the suite.

components.name: O-031 rewritten
components.responsibility: Rewrite the decision so later gates read the current placement. The used-space read now lives in Core, starts with the scan on its own thread, captures no scan memory and is never awaited by the scan. The guarantee is unchanged (a stalled share cannot hold the scan) and only the placement moved. Record that criterion 6 of SL-043 moved it.

components.name: Architecture rules, both twin forms
components.responsibility: The three rules declared by this design land in .taad/fitness.yaml AND in ArchitectureRulesTests, because eng/rules-parity.ps1 compares the two and fails on a rule present in one only.
components.key_interactions: Per Q-010, add to the existing rules file on trunk and never create it again.

key_decisions.decision: A link is exactly: reparse attribute set AND tag & 0x20000000. The junction/symlink/DFS list is dropped. DFS 0x8000000A dirs are now descended, and surrogate-tagged entries outside the old list (LX_SYMLINK, 0xA0000010 and the like) become Links that charge nothing.
key_decisions.rationale: This is agreed criterion 4 and the ONLY-UNDER condition of U-004. The risk spike walked 829K C: directories with this descend rule through DirectoryReader: 0 exceptions, 0 partial lists, only 5/363/1920. A descended DFS stub that fails lands in the existing unreadable record, which is never silent. It is one predicate plus a table, so an hour to revert. No DFS namespace was measured on this machine, so the DFS consequence is asserted by the criterion and not by a probe.

key_decisions.decision: The used-space read moves into Core (Scanning/VolumeSpace.cs), starts at scan start on its own background thread, and is published as ScanStore.VolumeUsed : Task<long?>. Neither the walk, the cancel nor the end of a scan ever waits on it. O-031's placement is superseded and its guarantee is kept.
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 6 says the scan records the figure alongside the tree, and O-031 exists so a stalled share cannot hold the scan. A never-awaited read on its own thread satisfies both, so nobody has to pick one. It has one consumer (MainWindow) and one doc paragraph. A Task rather than a nullable field lets the App keep 'appears when the volume answers' for slow shares and lets tests wait deterministically without finishing a C: scan.

key_decisions.decision: The volume thread captures only the TaskCompletionSource, never the ScanStore, and VolumeSpace.cs may not name ScanStore.
key_decisions.rationale: A read stalled on a dead mapped drive parks its thread for good. If that thread held the store it would pin a ~700 MiB scan (U-001) that the user has already discarded. The proposal's Start(root, store) shape had this hole. Passing the completion source instead costs nothing and is enforced by a rule.

key_decisions.decision: The source is GetDiskFreeSpaceExW (TotalNumberOfBytes - TotalNumberOfFreeBytes) by P/Invoke on the stripped 'X:\' root. It is not DriveInfo and not CIM/WMI.
key_decisions.rationale: This route was measured against Get-Volume: 30 of 30 in the bracket, median 0, max 40 KiB, no partition, reserved-storage or quota offset. It equals DriveInfo's figure to the byte. P/Invoke keeps the Scanning no-BCL rule intact and adds no package. The stripped form is what the spike called. Whether the \\?\ form is accepted was not measured, so it is not used.

key_decisions.decision: The App deletes VolumeInUse and awaits store.VolumeUsed on its existing post-scan thread. Display text, the root-failure condition and the report schema are unchanged.
key_decisions.rationale: If both the App and Core computed the figure, Core's value would be read by nobody. One source, one consumer.

key_decisions.decision: 'Drive root' means what the App already meant: exactly X:\ after stripping \\?\. Folder scans, UNC shares and mount-point folders complete the figure with null at once.
key_decisions.rationale: The rule moves without widening. A used-space figure on a folder scan would make the coverage gap meaningless. Completing null (not leaving the Task pending) matters, because the App would otherwise wait forever on every folder scan.

key_decisions.decision: Criterion 6's 'read at the same moment' is tested as a bracket: Get-Volume before the scan and after the figure lands, with 64 MiB of slack. The C: scan is cancelled once the figure lands rather than run to completion.
key_decisions.rationale: Reads from two processes cannot be simultaneous. A bracket absorbs monotone drift and the slack absorbs a write-then-delete inside about 3 s. It is the spike's A1/B/A2 method carried over. Cancelling keeps the test to seconds and inside memory, and shows a cancelled scan still carries the figure. powershell.exe (5.1) is used because it ships with Windows 10/11. The spike measured pwsh 7, so if 5.1's Get-Volume misbehaves unelevated, the test switches to pwsh with no design change.

key_decisions.decision: Criterion 1's reference is Directory.EnumerateFileSystemEntries over the \\?\ root with AttributesToSkip=0 and IgnoreInaccessible=false, on a link-free tree containing hidden entries. The non-elevation check reads TokenElevation and fails instead of skipping.
key_decisions.rationale: It uses a different information class from the scanner's extended-class listing, and the survey probe matched 14 of 14. The default EnumerationOptions skips Hidden|System, so an 'independent' reference on defaults could disagree with a correct scanner, or agree with one that also drops hidden entries. TokenElevation is what the criterion and spike name. IsInRole(Administrator) reports group membership, and a UAC-filtered admin is a member but not elevated.

key_decisions.decision: Errors 363 and 1920 are covered by classification rows only, as agreed. No real-tree fixture produces them.
key_decisions.rationale: The agreed check names a unit test. The recording path is generic (one code from ClassifyReadError to FolderDone) and the ACL test already proves it for 5. Forcing 1920 with a synthetic third-party reparse tag rests on unverified user-mode permissions, so it is a new slice if wanted.

key_decisions.decision: No app.manifest / longPathAware in this slice. The risk spike's no-go is compensated by a validate-time check on the published exe, not by anything in Core.Tests.
key_decisions.rationale: The no-go bites only if code opens a path over 260 characters without \\?\. This slice's App change opens nothing, and Core builds \\?\ paths through LongPath.cs. But testhost is long-path-aware and the published exe is not, so no Core test can notice a missing prefix. The obligation is to scan a >260-character tree through the published exe at validate and compare counts.

proposals.note: Only proposal handed over. Its shape is taken whole; the ScanStore capture in the volume thread is redesigned, and the stall test plus three rules are added. Its expert list and any over_engineering_flag were beyond the clipped portion.

payload.coherence_check: One proposal, no composition to check, and nothing here has survived a disagreement: the reviewer downstream should treat this as untested by any competing design. The first things to argue with are (1) the O-031 supersession, which puts a Task on the store and rewrites a decision the survey called deliberate, and (2) descending DFS directories, which the agreed criterion demands but no probe on this machine exercised. I checked the proposal's pieces against each other and against measurements. (a) Classifier vs existing guards: the change stays inside EntryClassifier, so OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute and its twin hold. Two EntryClassifierTests rows flip, and any other test encoding the old tag list must be found by grep, not assumed. (b) Volume read vs TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls: P/Invoke through Native, no DriveInfo, so it holds. (c) Volume read vs SL-042's memory budget: the store gains one completion source. That seam was where the proposal contradicted its own guarantee: Start(root, store) let a stalled thread pin the store. I redesigned it to pass only the completion source, enforced by a rule, and added a substituted-reader test that shows a scan ending while the figure is pending. (d) Two 'no figure' states: null means answered with nothing, and pending means the read has not returned. They are now a stated contract, and the App treats both as 'show nothing' and blocks neither the UI nor the next scan. (e) Criterion 1 asserts Completed and the volume test asserts a cancelled end, so they are separate tests and do not contradict. (f) Cut criteria 2 and 3 are untouched, and the classifier change cannot alter them because junction and symlink tags stay surrogate; the full suite run at build confirms it. (g) The testhost-versus-exe long-path no-go cannot be closed by a Core test, so it is carried as a validate-time case instead of being claimed. (h) Rules must exist in both fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests or rules-parity.ps1 fails. Everything builds and tests through eng/dotnet.ps1, because the machine has no SDK 10.

architecture_rules.name: the classifier does not list link tags; the surrogate bit is the rule
architecture_rules.because: A link is 'reparse attribute AND name-surrogate bit' (criterion 4, U-004). Re-listing tags brings back DFS as a link, so directories are silently skipped, and lets surrogate tags outside the list (LX_SYMLINK and others) be counted as files, so bytes are counted twice or charged to the wrong place.

architecture_rules.name: nothing in Core waits on the volume figure
architecture_rules.because: O-031 exists so a stalled share or dead mapped drive cannot hold a scan. One Wait, Result or await on the figure anywhere on the scan's path makes the scan never end when GetDiskFreeSpaceExW never returns, and the person sees a frozen progress bar. The App may wait on it because it does so on its own thread, and it is outside this glob.

architecture_rules.name: the volume read cannot hold a scan's memory
architecture_rules.because: A read stalled on an unreachable drive parks its dedicated thread indefinitely. If that thread's closure names the store, the discarded scan (~700 MiB at 5M rows, against ~136 MiB of headroom) stays alive for as long as the thread. The read is handed only the completion source.

cases.behaviour: scan a tree and compare the store with an independent recursive listing
cases.shape: folders AND files whose full paths cross 260 characters, deepest over 400, no links, in a non-elevated process
cases.why: The MAX_PATH branch is where a plain path is silently altered or refused. The comparison has to be against a listing built a different way (Directory.EnumerateFileSystemEntries over \\?\), not a hand-written expected list, and each entry has to sit once under its real parent (paths are rebuilt from the parent chain).

cases.behaviour: scan a tree and compare the store with an independent recursive listing
cases.shape: the tree contains a hidden file and a hidden folder
cases.why: The default EnumerationOptions skips Hidden|System. A reference built on defaults would either fail a correct scanner or agree with a scanner that also drops hidden entries. AttributesToSkip=0 is what makes the comparison independent.

cases.behaviour: confirm the test process is not elevated
cases.why: Criterion 1 requires the run to be as an ordinary user, and an elevated run would read folders an ordinary user cannot. The helper throws on a Win32 failure and never defaults to 'not elevated'. This shape cannot be fed without elevating the test host, and the spike measured testhost Medium in 2 of 2 valid runs. If a harness ever elevates it, the test goes red on purpose.

cases.behaviour: classify an entry as link or not
cases.shape: reparse attribute set and a surrogate-bit tag: junction 0xA0000003, symlink 0xA000000C (dir and file), LX_SYMLINK 0xA000001D file, 0xA0000010 dir
cases.why: The old code matched three tags. The last two rows are the ones the old rule got wrong: they were File and Folder, and bytes reached the totals through a link.

cases.behaviour: classify an entry as link or not
cases.shape: reparse attribute set and a non-surrogate tag: 0x9000201A, 0x9000401A, 0x9000601A, 0x9000E01A, tag 0, and DFS 0x8000000A (file and dir)
cases.why: These are descended or counted as files. 1.11M OneDrive entries on the dev machine carry cloud tags, and treating the reparse attribute alone as a link would drop them. DFS is the row that flips from Link to Folder, so it must be asserted, not merely removed.

cases.behaviour: classify an entry as link or not
cases.shape: the tag field holds a value with 0x20000000 set but the reparse attribute is clear (the fallback listing class carries EaSize there)
cases.why: Reading the tag before the attribute would turn an ordinary folder with such an EaSize into a Link and drop its whole subtree from the store.

cases.behaviour: record a folder that cannot be read and continue
cases.shape: read error 363 or 1920, with a cancel requested and not requested (5 and 995 alongside)
cases.why: The agreed check is a classification unit test. Errors 363 (cloud) and 1920 (tag-invalid) are the ones a descended non-surrogate reparse directory returns, and the spike saw 28 and 2 of them on C:. 995 must be Cancelled only under a requested cancel. The real-tree case for error 5 already exists (UnreadableFolderTests.AFolderThatCannotBeListedIsRecordedAndItsSiblingsAreCounted). A list failure after a successful open cannot be produced on NTFS as an ordinary user (0 in 829K directories).

cases.behaviour: record the used space of a drive-root scan
cases.shape: the system drive root, scan cancelled right after the figure lands, compared with Get-Volume read before and after
cases.why: The criterion compares with Get-Volume 'at the same moment', which two processes cannot do. The bracket with 64 MiB slack is what makes it decidable. It also shows a cancelled scan still carries the figure, and a full C: scan is not run.

cases.behaviour: record the used space of a scan
cases.shape: a folder scan (not a drive root)
cases.why: The figure must complete with null at once. A Task left pending would make the App wait forever after every folder scan, and a number on a folder scan would make the coverage gap meaningless.

cases.behaviour: decide whether a root is a drive root
cases.shape: C:\, c:\, \\?\C:\, C:\Users, \\server\share\, \\?\UNC\server\share\, a volume mounted on a folder
cases.why: The rule moves from the App to Core and must not widen. Only the first three are drive roots. A mount-point folder or share reporting the whole volume's used space would be a wrong figure with no error.

cases.behaviour: record the used space of a drive-root scan
cases.shape: a drive letter with no volume behind it, so GetDiskFreeSpaceExW returns false
cases.why: The failure must complete with null, never a faulted task, or the App's post-scan thread throws.

cases.behaviour: end a drive-root scan while the volume read is stalled
cases.shape: the substituted reader blocks and the scan is cancelled
cases.why: This is the only test of O-031's reason: the scan ends Cancelled with VolumeUsed still pending. Without it, a later .Wait() on the figure passes every other test.

cases.behaviour: scan a tree whose paths exceed 260 characters
cases.shape: run by the published single-file exe, which has no longPathAware manifest, not by the xUnit testhost, which is long-path-aware
cases.why: The risk spike's no-go: a plain long path opens in testhost and fails with error 3 in the exe. A Core test cannot see a missing \\?\ prefix, so validate must scan a >260-character tree through the published exe and compare the counts. If the launch contract cannot scan a given root, validate says so instead of passing.

cases.behaviour: show the used figure for a drive-root scan in the App
cases.shape: the App's outcome path reading store.VolumeUsed after MainWindow's own DriveInfo call is deleted
cases.why: A figure recorded in Core that no screen reads is this project's commonest defect. Build greps that VolumeInUse is gone and the outcome reads the store's figure. It runs the existing window cases unchanged, and if --report cannot show the figure, it says so.

contracts.name: EntryClassifier.Classify(attributes, reparseTag) -> EntryKind
contracts.notes: Link iff the reparse attribute is set AND the tag has the name-surrogate bit. The tag is ignored when the attribute is absent. Behaviour changes from the old rule: DFS dirs are now descended, and surrogate-tagged entries outside the old list are now Link and charge nothing.
contracts.error_cases: None: a total function. A descended non-surrogate folder that cannot be opened becomes an unreadable-folder record in Scanner, not here.

contracts.name: ScanStore.VolumeUsed : Task<long?>
contracts.notes: Never null and completes at most once. A value is used bytes (Total - TotalFree from GetDiskFreeSpaceExW at scan start) for a drive-root scan. A null result is a folder scan, a non-drive root or a failed read. Readable while the scan runs and after it ends, including a cancelled scan. Nothing in Core awaits it.
contracts.error_cases: A false return or exception on the volume thread completes null, never faulted. A read that never returns leaves it pending forever, so callers must not block a UI thread on it. The App waits on its existing post-scan thread and treats null and pending as 'show no figure'.

contracts.name: VolumeSpace.IsDriveRoot(root) and VolumeSpace.Start(root, completionSource, reader)
contracts.notes: Internal. IsDriveRoot is exactly 'X:\' after stripping \\?\ (the App's previous rule, moved not widened). Start completes null synchronously for anything else. Otherwise it runs the reader (default GetDiskFreeSpaceExW on the stripped root) on a dedicated background thread that captures only the completion source. The reader parameter is the test seam.
contracts.error_cases: TrySetResult makes a double completion a no-op. A reader exception becomes null.

contracts.name: Scanner.ClassifyReadError(error, cancelRequested)
contracts.notes: Unchanged behaviour: Unreadable for every nonzero code except 995 under a requested cancel. Newly pinned by rows for 363 and 1920 beside 5 and 995.

contracts.name: TokenElevation.IsElevated() (test helper)
contracts.notes: OpenProcessToken(TOKEN_QUERY) on the current process, then GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation, 4-byte buffer).
contracts.error_cases: A Win32 failure throws Win32Exception with the code. It never returns 'not elevated' by default.

contracts.name: Get-Volume probe from tests
contracts.notes: powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$v = Get-Volume -DriveLetter <L>; [long]($v.Size - $v.SizeRemaining)". The first call takes ~0.9 s (CIM warm-up, measured).
contracts.error_cases: A non-zero exit or unparsable stdout fails the test with the captured stderr. No retry and no skip.

contracts.name: --report <file> schema 1
contracts.notes: Unchanged. No field is added, renamed or removed. Only the App's internal source of the used figure moves, so eng/read-window.ps1 and WindowCases.ps1 need no change.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Clock synchronisation (Cristian's algorithm, NTP offset measurement)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: A remote value cannot be read at the same instant as the local reference, so bracket it: take the reference before and after the remote read, and accept the remote value inside [min, max] widened by a stated error. Criterion 6 does this with Get-Volume G1, the scan's recorded figure, then Get-Volume G2, accepted within 64 MiB of the bracket.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: It supplies a decision procedure for the criterion's 'read at the same moment', which two processes cannot do. It is a test-measurement technique only and shapes no component. The analogy is thin: bracketing two reads is ordinary practice, and the clock-sync name adds a citation, not a mechanism.

invariants.precondition: The bracketed figure and the reference measure the same quantity (Total - TotalFree from GetDiskFreeSpaceExW vs Get-Volume Size - SizeRemaining).
invariants.evidence: Spike volume-used-matches-get-volume: 30 of 30 inside the bracket, |B-A1| max 40,960 B, median 0, Size - TotalNumberOfBytes 0 in all 30, no quota. The survey's DriveInfo comparison was byte-equal.

invariants.precondition: Drift in used space during the window is monotone or bounded by the 64 MiB slack. Other processes (TAAD builds, a 300 MB SDK download into .dotnet/) write to the same drive.
invariants.evidence: Not measured under concurrent load. The bracket absorbs monotone drift, and only a write-then-delete larger than 64 MiB inside about 3 s could break it. The first runs of the test are where it shows.

invariants.precondition: The reference read is fast relative to the drift it must bracket.
invariants.evidence: Get-Volume's first call took ~0.88 s (CIM warm-up) and later calls ~55-6xx ms per the spike. The bracket is taken around the figure, and the figure lands within milliseconds of scan start.

prior_art.pattern: The name-surrogate bit (0x20000000) is the documented test for 'this reparse point stands for another named entity' (the IsReparseTagNameSurrogate macro). Non-surrogate tags (cloud, dedup, WOF, DFS) mark data handled by a filter.
prior_art.where: Windows SDK winnt.h; Microsoft Learn 'Reparse Point Tags'

prior_art.pattern: Recursive delete does not recurse into a directory whose reparse tag is a name surrogate. It removes the link itself, which avoids the 'recursive delete followed a junction into another tree' failure.

On Windows, Rust's FileType::is_symlink is true when the reparse attribute is set and the tag is a name surrogate, so walkers built on it never descend junctions or symlinks but do descend cloud placeholders.
prior_art.where: Rust std library, Windows fs implementation

prior_art.pattern: Follow symlinks and detect cyclic ones with a visited set. Rejected here: it charges link targets under the link's parent, still double-counts non-cyclic links, and needs a visited structure the store's memory headroom cannot afford.

new EnumerationOptions() defaults AttributesToSkip to Hidden|System, while the SearchOption overloads use compatible options that skip nothing. A reference listing built on the default can silently disagree with, or agree with a wrong, scanner.

Elevation is read from TOKEN_ELEVATION.TokenIsElevated via GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation). A UAC-filtered admin is a member of Administrators for deny only and is not elevated, so group-membership checks answer a different question.
Validate a remote reading by bracketing it between local reads taken before and after, and accept it inside that window plus a stated error.

taste_disagreements: Where the used-space figure lives. This design puts a Task<long?> on ScanStore, read by the App. The alternatives are a plain nullable on ScanResult (the read then has to be joined or polled at the end, which risks the stall) or leaving it in the App and rewording criterion 6 (which the survey said 'someone should decide'). A person may reasonably prefer the last; the design owns the agreed wording, so it moves the read.

VolumeSpace as its own file with an injectable reader, versus a private method in Scanner. The separate file lets the rule 'may not name ScanStore' have a file to point at. It is boundary placement, and neither answer changes a contract.
The 64 MiB slack on the Get-Volume bracket. It is inherited from the spike's method, and a tighter or looser bound is a judgement about how noisy this machine's drive is.
Classification rows for 363/1920 extend SynchronousIoCancelTests, as beside the existing 0/5/995 test, rather than a new ClassifyReadErrorTests file.

HardlinkTests and LinkTests (criteria 2 and 3, cut as present) and UnreadableFolderTests' ACL-deny test as the real-tree case for error 5.
LongPath.cs \\?\ prefixing, and the LongPathTests and TraversalTests patterns for building trees in %TEMP%.
The App's drive-root rule, display text and 'did not fail at the root' condition, moved rather than rewritten.
The spike's A1/B/A2 bracket method for Get-Volume, and its finding that GetDiskFreeSpaceExW matches Get-Volume.
ArchitectureRulesTests, .taad/fitness.yaml and eng/rules-parity.ps1 as the rule mechanism, plus eng/dotnet.ps1 for every build and test (the machine has no SDK 10).
